requiredFindings.summary: The snapshot neither records nor accounts for the root identity.
requiredFindings.details: The accepted plan records process_identity for each pid and accounts every pid inspected or queued while excluding only the root from by-pid targeting. The candidate pushes the root into the bounded queue but skips its identity read and both evidence counts, so a root-only snapshot consumes a slot while reporting queued=0 and inspected=0. Record and count the root as a distinct snapshot pid without adding it to kill.targets, and add root-only plus corrected boundary controls.

requiredFindings.summary: The provider's four-PID walk bound has no runtime control.
requiredFindings.details: The accepted D5-T4 control requires runtime boundary coverage at 4 for providers and 64 for tools. The candidate drives only the tool path; its provider assertion merely recomputes constants and would not catch walk_bound returning 64 for providers. Add a provider snapshot control for root plus three descendants completing and root plus four descendants reaching BoundReached and IncompletePlatformLimited.

requiredFindings.summary: The alive-root side of the required root-state distinction is not directly proved.
requiredFindings.details: The explicit ceiling control covers a held zombie through reap_blocked. The group-kill-failure case reaches an alive root because the fixture ignores SIGTERM, but it asserts neither ExitClass::Unreaped, distinct confirm evidence, absence of a by-pid root kill, nor absence of group signals after abandonment, and it does not clean up the surviving root. Add a direct bounded alive-root control with those assertions and cleanup.

nonBlockingObservations: Manifest and all 28 member hashes match; all 13 baselines match product commit d154eb002fc536855b9c831d0d6484bfaf5335d3, and the frozen authority files match their authority bytes.

The bounded production listings, original LaunchError settlement evidence, Exceeded and failure latching, reap-last ordering, TreeSwept fact mapping, and macOS versus Linux separation are otherwise present in the inspected source.
The conservative no-cgroup checker includes tracked and unignored Rust sources and tests under both source roots and explicitly makes no qualification claim.
